extracted.intended_audience: researchers, clinicians, and instrument developers conducting reliability and validity studies of assessment tools
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing and reporting the reliability (interrater, intrarater, test–retest) and validity (criterion, construct, face, convergent) of clinical or research measurement instruments using appropriate designs, rater procedures, and statistical metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrater reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistency/agreement of measurements made by different raters evaluating the same subjects or cases (appears across multiple studies as a primary outcome).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported with kappa statistics, intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), percentage agreement; interpretive labels used in the page include 'moderate', 'good', 'substantial', 'high', 'almost perfect'. Use multiple metrics to capture categorical vs continuous data. Examples: HOME FAST showed moderate interrater agreement; OSATS 1-page checklist κ = 0.53 (binary).

rubrics_metrics.name: Test–retest reliability (between-sessions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stability of measurements when the same instrument is administered to the same subjects at different times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported with ICCs or Kappas and percentage agreement. Example: HOME FAST test–retest reliability was reported as good; GEM scale had substantial to almost perfect test–retest agreement (κ ≥ 0.60).

rubrics_metrics.name: Intrarater reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistency of measurements when the same rater assesses the same subject on different occasions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported with ICC or Kappa. Examples: ALSFRS-R intrarater averaged Kappa coefficients 0.63–1.00; QHRFF intra-rater reliability assessed with Kappa/ICC thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical measure used to quantify reliability for continuous or ordinal measures; reported with point estimates and sometimes confidence intervals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different ICC forms (absolute agreement vs consistency) should be specified. Page examples interpret ICCs: 0.53 described as substantial/good (69% reliable), 0.73 as high interrater reliability (85% reliable). Use ICC for continuous scores like dynamometry, measurement areas, or total scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohen's Kappa / Weighted Kappa
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistic for interrater agreement on categorical items (Cohen's Kappa for pairs, extensions for multiple raters; weighted Kappa for ordered categories).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thresholds used on the page: κ > 0.4 as at least moderate; specific item-level κ values reported (e.g., κ = 0.38, κ = 0.54). Use weighted Kappa for ordered ratings (QHRFF, clinical scales).

rubrics_metrics.name: Percentage agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Simple proportion of cases in which raters gave the same rating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used alongside kappa/ICC because it is easy to interpret; reported in many studies (e.g., GEM mean percentage agreement 79% interrater, 83% test–retest). Note percentage agreement does not account for chance agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bland–Altman analysis / assessment of systematic bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Method to visualize agreement between two measurement methods or raters and to detect systematic bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compare methods (e.g., photographic analysis vs paper template for skin flap viability). Bland–Altman plots help show presence/absence of systematic bias even when correlation is high.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Metrics for criterion validity when an instrument's items are compared against a criterion/gold standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess criterion validity of items (QHRFF reported sensitivity/specificity/PPV; thresholds used like PPV > 0.7 considered at least moderate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion (criterion-related) validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which instrument scores correspond to a known gold standard or criterion measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed via correlations with the criterion, sensitivity/specificity/PPV, or comparison to established indices. Example: QHRFF criterion validity judged with PPV and comparisons; severity index correlated with Horn index and POSSUM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which an instrument measures the theoretical construct it purports to measure, often demonstrated via expected associations with related measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrated by associations with related outcomes (e.g., severity index associated with discharge status and length of stay; pain behavior frequencies correlated with self-reported pain). Use correlation analyses and hypothesis testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Face validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Expert judgment that instrument items appear to measure the intended construct and are clinically important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed by surveys of clinicians or stakeholders (e.g., FLEE face validity survey indicated high importance for tests). Face validity alone is weak but informative for instrument acceptance and practicality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure of how well items on a scale correlate to form a coherent construct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as Cronbach's alpha (e.g., surgical severity index standardized alpha = 0.8). Interpret in context; high alpha supports use of summed scores but may reflect redundancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coefficient of variation (CoV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Relative measure of dispersion of repeated measures, useful for comparing variability across measurement sites or raters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in ultrasound nerve measurements (CoV range 9.33%–22.5%). Lower CoV indicates more consistent measurement; report along with ICC for precision insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rater training and instrument-specific rater training
rubrics_metrics.description: Effect of training raters on the instrument-specific scoring conventions on reliability and differentiation of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structured training, explicit scoring conventions, and model training programs (e.g., GRID-HAMD training with videotaped interviews, instrument-specific rater training) improve interrater reliability, including for inexperienced raters. Report training procedures and pre/post training reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rater characteristics and experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Influence of rater professional background, experience, and prior affiliation on reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some studies show little influence of years of experience (bvFTD criteria), while others emphasize variability across rater backgrounds (HOME FAST used raters from nine professions). Report rater demographics and examine experience as a potential moderator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinding of raters
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of blinded evaluations to reduce bias and simulate independent assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blinded raters (no affiliation, unaware of training year) were used in OSATS evaluation to confirm interrater reliability. Blinding should be reported and used when possible to minimize expectancy or carryover bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detail and quality of source information (narrative length/evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: How the amount and clarity of case information or narratives influences rater agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shorter narratives (ROSIS) led to more rater disagreement than longer ICRP narratives in incident classification; implication: more detailed case information increases consistency across raters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of standardized/explicit scoring conventions and structured interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing standardized questions, definitions, and detailed scoring rules to reduce ambiguity and improve reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GRID-HAMD standardized explicit scoring conventions produced excellent interrater reliability for inexperienced and experienced raters. Recommendation: include structured interview guides and explicit scoring instructions in instrument design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate choice of statistical method and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Selecting and reporting the correct reliability/statistical metric for the data type (e.g., ICC for continuous, kappa for categorical), and specifying details (type of ICC, confidence intervals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Studies used ICC (with absolute agreement definition), Fleiss' kappa for multiple raters, free-marginal multirater kappa. Report which variant was used, report CIs, and complement with percentage agreement and other diagnostics when informative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsiveness / sensitivity to clinical change
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability of an instrument to detect clinically meaningful change over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed in ALSFRS-R where scale declined with time and correlated with global clinical impression of change; include longitudinal data and sensitivity analyses where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor analysis and factorial structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of exploratory or confirmatory factor analysis to evaluate dimensionality and construct structure of scales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ALSFRS-R factor analysis showed three-factor structure (neuromuscular, respiratory, bulbar) and factor loadings supported interpretation. Report factor loadings and rotation methods; use findings to justify scoring (sum vs subscales).

rubrics_metrics.name: Convergent/correlational validity across instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of correlation between the instrument under study and other established instruments measuring similar constructs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: ROBIS ratings correlated strongly with AMSTAR (r s = 0.76); MERSQI and NOS-E scores correlated (rho 0.49–0.72). Use correlation coefficients to demonstrate convergent validity and discuss implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of methodological quality checklists for study evaluation (e.g., QAREL)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessing the methodological quality of reliability studies using standardized checklists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The systematic review of knee physical tests evaluated methodological quality with the QAREL checklist (mean QAREL score reported). Use and report such checklists to contextualize confidence in reliability estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practicality, adaptability, and utility of the instrument
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of instrument length, ease of use, applicability across settings and professions, and usefulness for stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: QHRFF judged suitable for multiple at-risk populations with recommendations to remove weak items; retail store scoring system was weighted to emphasize healthy foods and reported as useful to health departments. Report feasibility, time burden, and adaptability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting of sample characteristics and study design
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear description of participant numbers, rater numbers and backgrounds, setting, and study design (cross-sectional, prospective, blinded) to allow interpretation and generalizability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: many abstracts report n for subjects and raters, whether raters were paired/blinded, and setting (e.g., simulation, community). Reliability depends on these design choices; report them fully.
